Name: Step Pyramid of Djoser
Overview: The Step Pyramid of Djoser is considered the earliest colossal stone building in Egypt and the first pyramid ever built, designed by the architect Imhotep for Pharaoh Djoser.

KeyFacts.Headline: Architect
KeyFacts.Description: Designed by Imhotep, the first recorded architect in history.

KeyFacts.Headline: Built
KeyFacts.Description: Circa 2667–2648 BC.

Name: Temple of Karnak
Overview: The Karnak Temple Complex is one of the largest religious sites ever built, dedicated to the Theban triad of Amun, Mut, and Khonsu. It features massive pylons, obelisks, and the famous Hypostyle Hall.

KeyFacts.Headline: Highlight
KeyFacts.Description: The Hypostyle Hall with 134 massive columns reaching 23 meters high.

KeyFacts.Headline: Timeline
KeyFacts.Description: Construction and expansion spanned over 1,500 years.

Name: Temple of Hatshepsut (Deir el-Bahari)
Overview: The Mortuary Temple of Hatshepsut is an architectural masterpiece built into the cliffs of Deir el-Bahari. It honors one of Egypt’s most successful female pharaohs.

KeyFacts.Headline: Built
KeyFacts.Description: Around 1479–1458 BC.

KeyFacts.Headline: Architect
KeyFacts.Description: Designed by Senenmut, Hatshepsut’s royal architect.

Name: Dendera Temple Complex
Overview: Dedicated to the goddess Hathor, the Dendera Temple is famous for its astronomical ceiling and detailed hieroglyphic reliefs. It dates back to the late Ptolemaic and Roman periods.

KeyFacts.Headline: Highlight
KeyFacts.Description: Astrological ceiling featuring the Dendera Zodiac.

KeyFacts.Headline: Period
KeyFacts.Description: Constructed during the Ptolemaic and Roman eras.

Name: Siwa Oasis
Overview: A remote oasis famous for its salt lakes, ancient ruins, and unique Berber culture. Siwa offers a blend of history, desert scenery, and traditional life.

KeyFacts.Headline: Distance from Cairo
KeyFacts.Description: Approximately 560 km southwest of Cairo.

KeyFacts.Headline: Famous Spot
KeyFacts.Description: Cleopatra’s Bath and the Temple of the Oracle of Amun.

Name: Mosque of Muhammad Ali
Overview: Built in the Ottoman style, the Mosque of Muhammad Ali dominates the skyline of Cairo. It is one of the city’s most famous landmarks, located inside the Citadel.

KeyFacts.Headline: Construction
KeyFacts.Description: Built between 1830 and 1848 by Muhammad Ali Pasha.

KeyFacts.Headline: Architectural Style
KeyFacts.Description: Modeled after the Blue Mosque in Istanbul.

Name: Luxor Temple
Overview: Located on the east bank of the Nile, the Luxor Temple was dedicated to the rejuvenation of kingship and is beautifully illuminated at night.

KeyFacts.Headline: Built
KeyFacts.Description: Around 1400 BC during the reign of Amenhotep III.

KeyFacts.Headline: Night Experience
KeyFacts.Description: Open at night for visitors to enjoy the illuminated ruins.

Name: Catacombs of Kom El Shoqafa
Overview: A historical archaeological site in Alexandria and one of the Seven Wonders of the Middle Ages, blending Egyptian, Greek, and Roman cultural elements.

KeyFacts.Headline: Era
KeyFacts.Description: Built in the 2nd century AD.

KeyFacts.Headline: Features
KeyFacts.Description: Underground burial chambers and Greco-Roman sculptures.

Name: Mount Sinai (Jebel Musa)
Overview: Mount Sinai is a sacred site in Christianity, Judaism, and Islam. It is believed to be the mountain where Moses received the Ten Commandments.

KeyFacts.Headline: Elevation
KeyFacts.Description: Approximately 2,285 meters above sea level.

KeyFacts.Headline: Visitor Tip
KeyFacts.Description: Many tourists climb at night to witness the sunrise.

Name: White Desert National Park
Overview: Known for its surreal white chalk formations shaped by wind erosion, the White Desert is one of Egypt’s most unique natural wonders.

KeyFacts.Headline: Rock Formations
KeyFacts.Description: Wind-carved limestone and chalk pillars resembling mushrooms and animals.

KeyFacts.Headline: Activities
KeyFacts.Description: Popular for camping and desert safaris under the stars.
